nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $S \subseteq R$. If some sequence in $R$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, then $S$ is infinite.
nodes.title: A set with a p-ordering is infinite

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. If $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$, then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$.
nodes.title: Building a p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then for every $n$, $v_n(a_n)$ is the least element of $\{v_n(x) : x \in S\}$.
nodes.title: Each term of a p-ordering attains the least valuation

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n \ge 1$ and every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: The stage-zero condition of a p-ordering is automatic

Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the definition of a p-ordering

nodes.title: Terms of a p-ordering lie in the set

nodes.title: Minimality of a p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. For every $x \in R$, the stage-$0$ prefix-product valuation of $x$ with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$ is $0$: the product is empty, so the ideal is all of $R$.
nodes.title: The stage-zero valuation vanishes

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
